clue.text: Blue book includes work about maize production

indicators.note: the pornography word takes the other pieces inside it, as a container holds its contents

parts.note: a blue book is a smutty one, so the pair stands for pornography, shortened as usual
OP is short for opus, a musical work
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A risqué book contains some writing on how corn is grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts OP and C after the first letter of PORN: P + OPC + ORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped kernels are something made from maize, a snack produced by heating the grain.

clue.text: David's work book

parts.note: King David was traditionally the author of the Psalms, and a bound volume of them is his work in book form

explanation.surface: A man named David has a workbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume of the Psalms, traditionally ascribed to King David, used in worship.

clue.text: A hill poem revised by Arnold

indicators.note: revised means the words are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Matthew Arnold reworked a poem about a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the title of a poem by Matthew Arnold, about the nightingale of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold wrote a poem with this title about the nightingale of Greek legend.

clue.text: Honour a leader of Haitian magic

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Haitian leader receives an honour for sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a form of West Indian sorcery or folk magic.

clue.text: Food makes us turn queer — one tin empty

indicators.note: queer in its old sense of odd or strange suggests the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
O, a zero, looks like an empty ring

explanation.surface: Eating makes us feel peculiar, as one can is found empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes us' only links; the letters of TURN, I, TIN and O are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is the supply of food needed for health and growth.

clue.text: Tropical tree outside old town yields liqueur

explanation.surface: Around an ancient settlement grows a tropical tree whose fruit makes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' means the letters of CACAO go round UR: C + UR + ACAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Curaçao is an orange-flavoured spirit named after the Caribbean island.

clue.text: Many a diamond in the jar

parts.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals, standing for many
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: Lots of diamonds are kept in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthenware pot or vessel is another name for this.

clue.text: Rude noise get the cane for it

definitions.meaning: a derisive sound made by blowing through the lips
the fruit grows on canes, and a pupil making the noise would be caned

explanation.surface: A child who blows a rude noise will be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a contemptuous blowing noise and a soft red fruit borne on canes.

clue.text: Hippy following?

parts.note: the call 'hip, hip' is followed by a shout of 'hooray', so this is what comes after the hips, not a flower child's fans

explanation.surface: Are there fans of hippies?
explanation.definitionFit: The shout of applause comes after the hip, hip in a celebration.

clue.text: Though nothing turns up, fast becomes rich

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: turns means the following word is read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or lavishly luxurious.

clue.text: Quick drink about four

explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, not dead.

clue.text: What brides take perhaps to USA ? Sure!

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether brides go to America, and is told yes.

clue.text: Extractor of the bit the bolter takes ?

definitions.text: Extractor of the bit the bolter takes ?

parts.words: Extractor of the bit the bolter takes ?
parts.note: a runaway horse takes the bit between its teeth; read instead the bolter as a fast eater, and the bit is a morsel lodged in teeth, which a small pointed stick removes

explanation.surface: Something removes the bit that a runaway horse grips in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed stick is used to dislodge bits of food caught between the teeth.

clue.text: Does the college boat move so clumsily ?

definitions.text: Does the college boat move so clumsily ?

parts.words: Does the college boat move so clumsily ?
parts.note: Oxford colleges once kept large houseboats on the river, and a lumbering movement is named after such a flat vessel

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the college's rowing boat really moves this awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a flat-bottomed river vessel, as kept by Oxford colleges, and a verb for shoving clumsily.

clue.text: Note the first she bird

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A musical note introduces the first woman, a she-bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'she-bird' is split: 'the first she' is EVE, and 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a female ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: It came madly drinking up gin — puzzling !

indicators.note: drinking means the rearranged letters take the other piece inside
madly means the letters go wild and are rearranged
in a down clue up means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone arrives crazily after downing gin, which is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' makes EMATIC from IT CAME; 'up' turns GIN to NIG; 'drinking' puts NIG after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is mysterious and hard to understand.

clue.text: Grave loss of fivepence out of sixpence

definitions.text: Grave loss of fivepence out of sixpence

parts.words: Grave loss of fivepence out of sixpence
parts.note: losing five of every six pence is a serious matter; read differently it describes an import that leaves a tiny remainder

explanation.surface: Someone laments losing almost all of a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Sixpence was a pre-decimal British coin; losing five pence of it leaves just a penny, a serious loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grave is serious or of great consequence.

clue.text: Concerning support of pools investment-here to stay

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits below, so this word comes after

parts.note: a perm is a permutation, a combination bet on the football pools
anent is an old word for concerning or about

explanation.surface: Something about backing a football pools bet that will last.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British betting game on match results; a perm is a set of combinations of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permanent is meant to last for ever.

clue.text: Dry your hands perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Instruction to dry one's hands.

clue.text: No pedlar, his customers are men of letters

definitions.text: No pedlar, his customers are men of letters

parts.words: No pedlar, his customers are men of letters
parts.note: a pedlar travels, whereas this trader stays in one shop, and those buying writing paper are letter-writers rather than authors

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who does not roam serves literary gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade name echoes 'stationary': originally a bookseller with a fixed stall, unlike a pedlar.
explanation.definitionFit: This shopkeeper sells paper, envelopes and pens to those who write.

clue.text: Maker of tea for five in Pacific islands on the river

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the islands

parts.note: Samoa is a group of islands in the Pacific

clue.text: Swift horse mastered him

explanation.surface: A fast horse got the better of its rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like 'fast' but is the satirist Jonathan Swift; his Houyhnhnms are horses who rule over brute humans.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the brutish humans are ruled by the rational horse race.

clue.text: See the old boy start to play tennis

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
each point in tennis starts with a serve

explanation.surface: Watch the old fellow begin a game of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Palindromic calling of a musical heroine

clue.text: Challenged many a communist

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, many

clue.text: An account concerning the German snakes

parts.note: on can mean about or concerning, as in a talk on art
das is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a report about German snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large constricting serpents of South America.

clue.text: Hugh sounds a caution !

definitions.meaning: the name Hugh is pronounced like hue, a colour, so this is a colour
the light before red on a traffic signal warns drivers to stop

clue.text: Took a pig-got away with the beast !

clue.text: Reveal bit replaced is genuine

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a new order

clue.text: A large number of us in this affair
